title: @home café, classic Akihabara maid café
titleJa: あっとほぉーむカフェ
summary: The best-known maid café chain in Akihabara; maids greet you with 'Welcome home, Master/Princess'. You order food or a drink, the maids cast the 'moe moe kyun' spell on it, and you can buy an instant photo (cheki) with a maid.
why: It is the easiest, most beginner-friendly way to see the maid café culture you see in anime, with English menus and card/Alipay/WeChat payment.
cost: Admission ¥850 (ages 23–59; ¥600 ages 19–22) + at least 1 drink (¥720–900). Drink course incl. cheki ¥1,690; food course ¥2,810; full course ¥3,810. Extra cheki ¥870 (large ¥1,080). Total about ¥2,500–4,700.
winterNote: Indoor, open all year. Maids change costumes for seasonal 'cos days'. Weekends and evenings have a queue; use the at-Entry queue ticket or at-PASS reservation on the site. Electronic money (IC) payment ends Oct 2026; cards, PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay still OK.

places.ja: あっとほぉーむカフェ ドンキ店
あっとほぉーむカフェ AKIBAカルチャーズZONE店

photoQuery: Akihabara maid cafe Don Quijote building

experience.hook: Maids greet you in chorus and draw on your omurice in ketchup.
moments: Hear the whole café call 'Welcome home, Master!' as you step in and get your at-home key card.
Order the Hiyoko-san omurice and ask the maid to draw a picture on it in ketchup.
Make heart hands and chant 'moe moe kyun' with your maid to make the food 'tastier'.
Pick a maid and pose for a cheki photo; she decorates it with drawings at your table.
experience.tip: The Drink Course (¥1,690) already includes one cheki. It is the cheapest full experience if you are not hungry.

title: Maidreamin, maid café with stage shows
titleJa: めいどりーみん 秋葉原本店
summary: Big maid café chain with 7 shops in Akihabara, open until 23:00. Every shop has a small stage where maids sing and dance, and first-timers get a 'Maidreamin passport'.
why: Loud, bright and fun for a first visit, and the late hours fit an evening after a full day of anime spots.
cost: Entry ¥880 per hour (adult) + food/drink. Official average: ¥1,500 soft drink only, ¥2,000–2,500 with food, ¥2,500–3,500 with alcohol and a live show. Photo with a maid is extra.
winterNote: Indoor, open every day. Honten: Mon–Fri 11:30–23:00, Sat/Sun/holidays 10:30–23:00. No table or service charge. Payment: cash, cards, PayPay, WeChat Pay, Alipay. Reservation form on the site.

places.ja: めいどりーみん 秋葉原本店
めいどりーみん Heaven's Gate

experience.hook: Get a passport to the 'dream country' and watch maids perform live.
moments: Receive your Maidreamin passport and choose the name the maids will call you.
Say the spell 'oishiku nare, moe moe kyun' together with the maid over your drink.
Watch a maid song-and-dance show on the small stage between orders.
Take a commemorative photo with the maid you like before you 'leave the country'.
experience.tip: Entry is charged per hour, so order at once and watch the clock. For a bigger show, pick the Heaven's Gate live restaurant.

title: Cure Maid Café, the first maid café
summary: Opened in 2001, it calls itself Japan's first maid café. It is calm: classic long maid uniforms, good tea and scones, and a changing anime collaboration menu.
why: A quiet, historic spot for anime fans; it appears as a model in 'Love Live!' and 'Saekano' and always runs an anime collab.
cost: No entry charge found on the official site. Tea ¥770; food/collab menus extra. About ¥1,500–3,000.
winterNote: Open 11:00–20:00 daily (food L.O. 19:00). Moved: now in Onoden Bldg 4F (Gee! Store Akiba) by the station. Numbered tickets when busy; seat reservation only for paid 'supporter card' members. Collab cafés change about every 2 weeks; check what runs on Jan 20, 2027.
anime: Love Live! and Saekano (How to Raise a Boring Girlfriend) use it as a model; rotating official anime collab menus

experience.hook: Drink real tea where the maid café started, back in 2001.
moments: Ride the Onoden escalator to 4F and walk through the Gee! Store to the café.
Order a pot of Darjeeling or smoky Lapsang souchong from the tea list, ¥770.
Try a scone or waffle while maids in long classic dresses serve quietly.
Check the collab menu and goods of whatever anime runs that fortnight.
experience.tip: Photos of your food are fine, but keep staff and other guests out of the frame, and no video.

title: Cafe Mai:lish, quiet classic maid café
titleJa: カフェ メイリッシュ
summary: One of the older Akihabara maid cafés, calm and relaxed. No table charge: one order per 90 minutes, and the tea is certified by the Japan Tea Association.
why: A more authentic, less showy maid café for when the loud chains feel too much; no entry fee keeps it cheap.
cost: No table charge; 1 order per 90 min. About ¥1,000–2,500.
winterNote: Closed on Wednesdays, so NOT on day 2 (Wed Jan 20, 2027). Mon/Tue/Thu 14:00–22:00, Fri–Sun/holidays 12:00–22:00. Every Thursday is 'Classical Maid Day' (day 3 evening fits). Phone reservations only on weekdays, up to 1 month ahead; no reservations on weekends.

experience.hook: A calm maid café where nobody rushes you: one order buys 90 minutes.
moments: Climb to the 2nd floor of FH Kyowa Square on Sotokanda 3-chome.
Order tea and scones; on Thursdays the maids wear classic uniforms with a special tea menu.
Charge your phone at the table and rest your legs after the Akihabara crowds.
Collect a stamp for each ¥1,000 you spend on the original stamp card.
experience.tip: Go on Thursday evening (day 3) for Classical Maid Day. Ask staff first before you photograph your food.

title: Swallowtail butler café, Ikebukuro
titleJa: 執事喫茶 スワロウテイル
summary: A Victorian-style tea salon near Otome Road where butlers in tailcoats serve you. You pick your teacup from over 50, and eat a set meal or afternoon tea.
why: The elegant 'reverse' of a maid café, famous in otome and anime culture; men are welcome too.
cost: 1 set per person is required: ¥5,400 (e.g. pasta + salad + drink, or scones + savoury + dessert tea set); dinner course ¥7,900. Cash or credit card only (no e-money).
winterNote: Advance web reservation with an account is required; walk-in only if there is a same-day cancellation ('today's free seats' on the site). Tea time 10:30–18:15, dinner 18:30–21:15. Arrive 50+ min late = refused and cancellation fee. Menu changes monthly; book as soon as January dates open.

experience.hook: A butler opens the door and calls you home to a Victorian mansion.
moments: Wait by the basement entrance until the doorman checks your booking and a butler escorts you in.
Choose your teacup from more than 50 in the cup selection.
Eat the monthly set, like scones with two jams and creams, or seasonal pasta.
Relax to the end; a butler comes 20–30 minutes before your time ends to settle the bill.
experience.tip: Absolutely no photos inside, with no exceptions. Ask the doorman where you may photograph the entrance.

title: Maid idol live show night
titleJa: めいどりーみん LIVE RESTAURANT Heaven's Gate
summary: Maidreamin's 60-seat 'live restaurant' next to Akihabara station, built around a stage. Maids perform idol-style songs and dances while you eat and drink.
why: The closest thing to an idol concert-bar in one easy evening, and it stays open until 23:00.
cost: Entry ¥880 per hour + food/drink; about ¥2,500–3,500 with a drink and a show (official average for 'drinks and live').
winterNote: Open daily: Mon–Fri 11:30–23:00, Sat/Sun/holidays 10:30–23:00. Event nights (birthdays, battles between shops) are the busiest; check the event page for Jan 2027 and reserve on the site.

experience.hook: Eat dinner while maids put on a live idol show on stage.
moments: Take the lift to 6F of the building by the Electric Town exit.
Order a drink and food, then join the 'moe moe kyun' spell with the whole room.
Wave along as maids sing and dance on the stage, like at a small idol live.
Walk out after 22:00 into the lit-up Chuo-dori signs.
experience.tip: Look at the event calendar: a shop 'battle' or a maid's anniversary night gives the biggest show.

title: Otome Road and Animate Café
titleJa: 乙女ロード・アニメイトカフェ池袋
summary: Ikebukuro's Otome Road is the fan street for female anime fans. Eat at an official Animate Café anime collab and drink a 'Gratte' latte with a character printed on the cream.
why: Real anime collab food and goods in one short walk, with the Animate Ikebukuro main store next door.
cost: Collab café: about ¥2,000–3,000 (check each event). Gratte latte: about ¥1,000 (check). No reservation needed for Gratte.
winterNote: Collab titles change every few weeks; check animatecafe.jp in Dec 2026 for Jan 2027 events. Some collabs need an online seat reservation, others are 'free entry'. Gratte at Animate Ikebukuro main store 10:00–20:00; numbered tickets when busy.

places.ja: アニメイトカフェ池袋
執事喫茶 スワロウテイル

anime: Changing official collabs (whatever runs in Jan 2027)

experience.hook: Drink a latte with your favourite character printed on the foam.
moments: Walk Otome Road past shops full of character goods and doujinshi.
Order a Gratte and photograph the character printed on the cream before it melts.
Eat a themed collab dish and get a random bonus coaster or card.
Browse the floors of the Animate Ikebukuro main store for goods.
experience.tip: Pick the collab first on animatecafe.jp, then check if it needs a timed reservation. Many collabs sell out on the first days.

title: Pokémon Café Tokyo, Nihonbashi
summary: The official Pokémon café in Nihonbashi Takashimaya. You eat Pokémon-shaped food, and Pikachu comes out for a short live show.
why: A playful, very photogenic meal for anime and game fans, with English and simplified Chinese menus.
cost: About ¥2,500–4,000 per person for a dish, a drink and a dessert (estimate; check menu).
winterNote: Reservation only, via the official site; opening time for bookings can change (it is usually about one month ahead, check the news page). Same-day seats only from cancellations at the door. Open 10:30–21:00, L.O. 20:30.

experience.hook: Pikachu walks out and dances beside your table.
moments: Go up to 5F of the Takashimaya East building near Tokyo Station.
Order a Pokémon-shaped dish and a souvenir-menu drink that comes with a café-only item.
Watch the Pikachu show, about 10 minutes long.
Buy café-only goods in the shop before your 90 minutes end.
experience.tip: Set a reminder for the day bookings open; slots go in minutes. Each email address can book only one slot.

title: Kirby Café at Tokyo Skytree
summary: The official Kirby café in Tokyo Solamachi at the foot of Skytree. Food and sweets look like Kirby and his friends.
why: Cute, funny food for game fans, and you can join it with the Skytree view.
winterNote: Reservation needs an account (since Aug 2026 slots). Slots for a month opened on the 10th of the month before in 2026 (so Jan 2027 slots probably from about Dec 10, 2026, check). Max 3 bookings per month per shop; photo ID checked at the door. Open 10:00–22:00.

experience.hook: Eat a Kirby-shaped meal right under Tokyo Skytree.
moments: Find the café on Solamachi East Yard 4F, next to the Kirby Café The Store.
Order a Kirby dish and a dessert shaped like a Kirby character.
Photograph the food before you eat it; it looks too cute to cut.
Buy café-only goods at the store next door.
experience.tip: Come 10 minutes early with photo ID; the name on the booking must match.

title: Super Potato retro games and arcade
titleJa: スーパーポテト 秋葉原店
summary: A famous retro game shop on 3 floors with Famicom, Mega Drive and much more. The top floor is a small arcade with old cabinets and Japanese sweets (dagashi).
why: Old-school Japanese game culture next to the maid cafés; play a few ¥100 arcade games between cafés.
cost: Free to enter; arcade games from about ¥100; games and goods extra.
winterNote: Open every day 11:00–20:00. Kitabayashi Bldg 3F/4F/5F, next to the @home café main shop.

experience.hook: Walk into a shop packed floor to ceiling with Famicom cartridges.
moments: Go up to 3F and 4F, where the shelves are full of boxed retro games.
Look for old consoles, Famicom carts and rare handheld LSI games.
Play a round on an old arcade cabinet on 5F.
Buy a cheap dagashi sweet before you leave.
experience.tip: Check the back of the box for NTSC-J region before you buy a game to play at home.

title: Maid café night in Sapporo
titleJa: めいどりーみん 札幌狸小路店
summary: Maidreamin's 60-seat Sapporo shop on the covered Tanukikoji shopping street. Same maid show and spells as Akihabara, open until 23:00.
why: If you skip maid cafés in busy Tokyo, this is an easy, warm evening stop in snowy Sapporo.
winterNote: Open daily 11:30–23:00. Tanukikoji is a covered arcade, so the walk is dry in snow. Sapporo Snow Festival 2027 dates: check (usually early Feb). Pin is Tanukikoji 4-chome (shop address: Minami 2-jo Nishi 4-10-2, Shimizu Bldg 6F).

experience.hook: Warm up from the Sapporo snow with a maid café spell.
moments: Walk the covered Tanukikoji arcade to the 4-chome block.
Take the lift to 6F of the Shimizu Building.
Chant 'moe moe kyun' over a hot drink with the maid.
Watch the stage show, then walk to Susukino for ramen.
experience.tip: Go after dinner; it is open to 23:00 and the evening shows are the liveliest.

title: Character latte at Animate Sendai
titleJa: アニメイトカフェグラッテ アニメイト仙台
summary: A small Gratte counter inside Animate Sendai, by Sendai Station. You drink a latte with an anime character printed on the cream and browse the anime shop.
why: A quick 30-minute anime stop in Sendai before or after gyutan dinner.
winterNote: Animate Sendai is in EBeanS 7F by Sendai Station, indoor. Gratte hours 11:00–19:00 (L.O. 18:45). Titles change; check the Gratte event list for Jan 25, 2027.

experience.hook: Drink a latte with an anime character printed on top.
moments: Walk from Sendai Station west exit to EBeanS and go up to 7F.
Choose a character from the current collab and order the Gratte.
Take a photo of the printed cream before you drink.
Browse the Animate shop for manga and character goods.
experience.tip: L.O. is 18:45, so do it before gyutan dinner, not after.
